title: Gemini CLI discontinued, replaced by Antigravity CLI
description: Google announced Gemini CLI will stop working from June 18, 2026. The tool is being replaced by Antigravity CLI, positioned as a successor with multi-agent support. Enterprise users with Gemini Code Assist licenses retain access. The shutdown affects individual users and free tiers.

I stopped using Google products due to their propensity for killing them off. I continue to be proven correct
Welcome to the Google graveyard, Gemini CLI. Not that it will be missed much. Using it was the worst experience out of any harness
I've been a happy user of Gemini CLI. What makes it incomprehensibly bad?
Unsubscribed from Google Ultra, moving to Claude Max
Antigravity CLI is a disaster and half baked product
This is the Google messaging problem all over again. Now Meets Chat is Hangouts again!

title: June 9, 2026 release notes and cybersecurity features update
description: Claude Code updated with new cybersecurity features including /security-review command. Release notes documentation updated on June 9, 2026 reflecting changes to agent usage plans announced on June 15th.

title: Codex CLI 0.136 and 0.138.0 released with major improvements
description: OpenAI released Codex CLI version 0.136 with 129 total changes including 4 security fixes, 24 new features, 41 improvements, and 26 bug fixes. Version 0.138.0 followed with scrollbar alignment improvements, animated diff stat alignment, and better first-run suggestion adjustments. Added GPT-5.5 support, Chrome extension, and remote control capabilities.

title: Cursor 2.0 with Design Mode, Multi-select Editing, and Enhanced SDK
description: Cursor launched Design Mode in browser allowing users to click, draw, or describe UI changes by voice. Added multi-select editing for code and layout, auto-review run mode, and significant SDK improvements including custom tools, JSONL stores, nested subagents, and auto-review capabilities. Enterprise organizations feature also introduced.

community_feedback.quote: Cursor 2.0 is amazing well done to the team. Plan mode is a game changer too
Despite a lot of negativity, Cursor 2.0 is amazing
I'm going to start by saying I really like the well engineered AI handling. Functionally, cursor 2.0+ is not concerning

title: Major billing model transition to usage-based pricing
description: GitHub Copilot moved from request-based billing to usage-based billing using 'Copilot Credits' system for all plans. Copilot Code Review now consumes GitHub Actions minutes in addition to AI Credits. New user-level budget controls and Copilot Max upgrade launched.

community_feedback.quote: End of an Era [June 1, 2026] - GitHub Copilot models and prices
Starting June 1, 2026, GitHub is moving Copilot from request-based billing to usage-based billing. Users expressed frustration about losing the predictable $10/month flat rate
What a joke regarding the new token-based billing
Why should I pay $10 and be forced to use it by the end of the month, while I can pay $10 and have it...

title: Enterprise features and Windows VM native support
description: Devin announced major enterprise features and developer improvements including autofocus on confirmation buttons in archive dialogs, plan artifact button polish, configurable CI status features, and native Windows VM support for building, running, and testing code.
